deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the draft continuation of Riemann's 1859 letter, probably to Weierstrass, which was printed posthumously as 'Beweis des Satzes, dass eine einwerthige mehr als 2n-fach periodische Function von n Veränderlichen unmöglich ist' (Crelle 71, 1870; Werke). The previous page sets up a single-valued function f of n complex variables x_ν with period systems a_μ = (a_μ^1, …, a_μ^n), μ = 1, …, 2n. One writes x_ν = Σ_μ a_μ^ν ξ_μ/(2π) with real ξ_μ, so the 2n real ξ's are coordinates on C^n ≅ R^{2n}. The domain 0 ≤ ξ_μ < 2π (normalised on this page to 0..1) is a fundamental domain for the first 2n periods.

(A) Pigeonhole step (top of page and the redraft at the bottom). Divide each ξ-interval [0,1) into q equal parts. The fundamental cell of the lattice Λ = Z a_1 + … + Z a_{2n} then splits into q^{2n} subcells, in each of which every ξ varies by at most 1/q. (The page has the exponent written as 'q^n'-like; the count over 2n real coordinates must be q^{2n}.)

Suppose f has a further period a_{2n+1}. Take the points k·a_{2n+1}, k = 0, 1, …, q^{2n}, and reduce each modulo Λ into the cell. These are more than q^{2n} points that are congruent modulo all 2n+1 periods. If no two of them are congruent modulo Λ, two must still fall in the same subcell. Their difference is a period Σ_{μ≤2n} m_μ a_μ + m_{2n+1} a_{2n+1} ≠ 0 whose ξ-coordinates are all at most 1/q. Since q is arbitrary, f has arbitrarily small periods, so it would be unchanged along some real direction. This is the degenerate case: f is a function of fewer than n linear expressions in the x's. Otherwise some multiple of a_{2n+1} lies in Λ, i.e. there is an integer relation Σ_{μ=1}^{2n+1} a_μ^ν m_μ = 0.

(B) Lemma: basis extension. Let m_1, …, m_{2n} be integers without common divisor and b_1 = Σ m_μ a_μ. Then there are 2n−1 further period systems b_2, …, b_{2n} with Z⟨a⟩ = Z⟨b⟩ ('congruence modulo the a's is identical with congruence modulo the b's'). The proof is by successive gcd steps:
- Let ϑ_1 = gcd(m_1, m_2) and choose integers α, β with β m_1 − α m_2 = ϑ_1 (my sign normalisation; see errors).
- Put c_1 = (m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2)/ϑ_1 and b_{2n} = α a_1 + β a_2.
- The transformation matrix [[m_1/ϑ_1, m_2/ϑ_1], [α, β]] has determinant 1. Hence a_1 = β c_1 − (m_2/ϑ_1) b_{2n} and a_2 = −α c_1 + (m_1/ϑ_1) b_{2n}.
- So {a_1, a_2} can be replaced by {c_1, b_{2n}}.
- Next let ϑ_2 = gcd(ϑ_1, m_3), c_2 = (ϑ_1 c_1 + m_3 a_3)/ϑ_2, with a complementary system b_{2n−1}; and so on.
- At the end, c_{2n−1} = Σ m_μ a_μ / gcd = b_1.

Each step is unimodular, so the volume of the periodically repeating domain is unchanged.

(C) Reduction. Apply the lemma to the first 2n coefficients of the relation, after dividing out their gcd p. The relation becomes p b_1 = q a_{2n+1} with gcd(p, q) = 1 (the struck '+' was evidently changed to '−'). Choose γ, δ with γq + δp = 1. Then γ b_1 + δ a_{2n+1} = (γq + δp) b_1/q = b_1/q. Conversely b_1 = q·(b_1/q) and a_{2n+1} = p·(b_1/q). So all combinations of a_1, …, a_{2n+1} are integer combinations of b_1/q, b_2, …, b_{2n}, and the cell volume is divided by the integer q.

(D) Iteration. Each further period not already in the current lattice either produces arbitrarily small periods, or is absorbed into a new 2n-element basis while the cell volume drops by an integer factor ≥ 2. The volume cannot shrink indefinitely unless some dimension of the cell becomes infinitely small. In that case f is a function of n−1 (or n−2, …) linear combinations of the variables. Hence in the non-degenerate case the process stops: all periods are integer combinations of 2n of them. A single-valued, non-degenerate function of n variables therefore cannot be more than 2n-fold periodic.

A marginal remark notes that this presumes the n equations determining the ξ's are independent; the exceptions are 'easy to handle'. The lower part of the page contains closing courtesies of the letter ('entschuldigen Sie gütigst … flüchtig hingeworfenen Zeilen …'), several redrafts of the conclusion, and a redraft of the pigeonhole paragraph.
errors: Number of subcells: the period cell is 2n-real-dimensional, so subdividing each ξ into q parts gives q^{2n} cells, not q^n. Either the transcription misreads the exponent or Riemann slipped. The argument works with q^{2n}, using q^{2n}+1 multiples of a_{2n+1}.

Sign conventions in the Bezout step are inconsistent as transcribed. With b_{2n} = α a_1 + β a_2, the stated inverse a_2 = −α c_1 + (m_1/ϑ_1) b_{2n} requires β m_1 − α m_2 = ϑ_1, and then a_1 = β c_1 − (m_2/ϑ_1) b_{2n}. The transcription's 'α m_1 − β m_2 = ϑ_1' and '+ (m_2/ϑ_1) b' do not match. This is a harmless sign slip or misreading.

In (C) the relation must read p b_1 − q a_{2n+1} = 0 (i.e. a_{2n+1} = p b_1/q) for γ b_1 + δ a_{2n+1} = b_1/q to follow from γq + δp = 1. With p b_1 + q a_{2n+1} = 0 one would need γq − δp = 1. The struck '+' suggests Riemann corrected this.

The termination argument is only sketched. That the volume cannot become arbitrarily small without infinitesimal periods (equivalently, discreteness of the period group implies it is a lattice of rank ≤ 2n) is asserted rather than proved. Riemann himself calls the lines 'flüchtig hingeworfen'. The degenerate cases ('Ausnahmen') are waved off as easy.

results.what: Pigeonhole argument: a further period beyond 2n independent ones yields either arbitrarily small periods or an integer linear relation among the 2n+1 period systems
results.modern_name: Dirichlet box principle / simultaneous Diophantine approximation; discrete subgroups of R^{2n} have rank ≤ 2n
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (box principle, 1842); Jacobi (1834/35) for the one-variable case of no triply periodic functions

results.what: A primitive integer vector (m_1..m_{2n}) can be completed to a unimodular basis change, via successive gcd/Bezout steps
results.modern_name: Extension of a primitive vector to a basis of Z^k (unimodular completion); elementary lattice basis reduction

results.what: A single-valued non-degenerate function of n complex variables has at most 2n independent periods: every period is an integer combination of 2n of them, otherwise the function depends on fewer than n linear forms
results.modern_name: Structure of period groups: the period group of a non-degenerate meromorphic function on C^n is a lattice of rank ≤ 2n (Jacobi–Riemann–Weierstrass theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (letter to Weierstrass, 1859; published Crelle 71, 1870) and Weierstrass; Jacobi for n=1

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of Riemann's well-known letter to Weierstrass on the impossibility of more than 2n-fold periodic functions of n variables. It was published in Crelle 71 (1870) and in his Werke. The mathematics is his published argument; only draft variants, sign slips and the juxtaposition with the prime-number cover letter are of minor archival interest.

If a_{2n+1} = p*b1/q and gamma*q + delta*p = 1, then gamma*b1 + delta*a_{2n+1} = b1/q
Bezout coefficients exist (example), giving s*12 + t*18 = gcd = 6 as used for theta_1

transcription_corrections: 'Gebiet in q^n Theile zerfällt' and 'mehr als q^n': mathematically this must be q^{2n}; the image exponent looks like '2n' rather than 'n' in at least the first instance.
'Durch successive q^n malige Anwendung' should likely read q^{2n}-malige.
Bezout condition: likely 'β m_1 − α m_2 = ϑ_1' rather than 'α m_1 − β m_2 = ϑ_1'.
The inverse formula should read a_1^ν = β c_1^ν − (m_2/ϑ_1) b_{2n}^ν; the sign before the m_2 term appears to be a minus.
'p b_1^ν [-+-] q a_{2n+1}^ν = 0': the '+' is struck, presumably replaced by '−'.
'δ p [-+-] + q γ = 1': the condition is γq + δp = 1 (a stray struck sign only).

'Es ist nun auch zu zeigen' / 'Wir zeigen zunächst leicht beweisen' are garbled; the text reads approximately 'Es ist nun noch zu zeigen, dass, wenn zwischen den 2n+1 Modulsystemen ganzzahlige Gleichungen Σ a_μ^ν m_μ = 0 stattfinden, ... Wir wollen zunächst beweisen, dass ...'.
The page number '27' at right margin is a folio number embedded in the text, not part of the mathematics.
